title: weekend reads ghost data centers critical minerals backlash treasurys debt boom 2026 09 04
author: Anna Szymanski
text:
Sept 4 (Reuters) - Looking for inspiration? Every Friday, Weekend Reads rounds up what the Reuters Open Interest team has been reading, watching and listening to.
This ​week's picks cover AI's expanding footprint, ghost data centers, critical minerals, China's energy transition and ‌more.
This weekend, we're reading...
MIKE DOLAN, ROI Finance & Markets Columnist: This infographic by the Pew Research Center
, opens new tab
, a U.S. think tank, illustrates how much of the web's written content is now produced by AI — an alarmingly large share.
RON BOUSSO, ROI Energy Columnist: Our Reuters ​colleague Laila Kearney discovered that a huge number of U.S. data centers seeking connections to ​the power grid are phantoms. This could have a big impact on forecasts ⁠for power demand and investment needs in the sector.
ANDY HOME, ROI Metals Columnist: This piece from ​international affairs think tank Chatham House
, opens new tab
 is a timely call for the mining industry to remain focused on responsible ​practices. The race for critical minerals has pushed environmental, social and governance issues down the collective agenda, but allegations of human rights abuses are rising — up 73% in 2025 — as governments and communities push back.
GAVIN MAGUIRE, ROI Global Energy ​Transition Columnist: The Boston Consulting Group
, opens new tab
 considers which aspects of China's energy transition could be adapted elsewhere — ​and the various trade-offs involved.
CLYDE RUSSELL, ROI Asia Commodities and Energy Columnist: This analysis from think tank Asia House
, opens new tab
 examines various alternatives ‌for ⁠getting oil and gas out of the Middle East amid the ongoing Strait of Hormuz crisis. (Disclosure: I'm quoted in the article and helped the author with it.)
We're listening to...
ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: Reuters Breakingviews Global Editor Peter Thal Larsen recently sat down with journalist and author Ed Conway to discuss how trade ​chokepoints — from U.S. tariffs to ​Chinese rare earths ⁠export restrictions and beyond — have shaped global commerce, and why such efforts to restrict commerce rarely endure.
And we're watching...
JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: The ​borrowing binge to finance the AI boom is, well, booming. But to ​what extent is ⁠AI debt issuance contributing to the surge in Treasury yields, and is the risk to financial markets overblown? Rebecca Patterson and Sebastian Mallaby at the Council on Foreign Relations discuss this and the wider U.S. ⁠fiscal situation ​with Torsten Slok, partner and chief economist at Apollo, in ​the latest episode of The Spillover podcast
, opens new tab
.
